events.factual_description: Westminster Presbyterian Church's official Blue Monday Blues schedule lists '20th Blue Monday Blues Anniversary & Farewell to Rev. Brian' for Monday, September 21, 2026. The church states that Blue Monday runs from 6:00 to 9:00 PM with $10 admission payable by cash or credit card, and names Brian Lenair on saxophone, Chuck Carthan on bass, Peter Frassrand on piano, Kenny Powell on drums, and Tiya Ade on vocals. The same official schedule says this anniversary will be the final Blue Monday Blues event in the long-running program's Hamilton era and invites the community to celebrate the transition from one era to the next. Westminster identifies Rev. Brian Hamilton as pastor and as president of the Southwest Renaissance Development Corporation that runs the church's jazz and blues ministry. A September 1, 2026 Southwester report says Hamilton is retiring on September 27 after thirty years at Westminster and describes weekly Jazz Night and Blue Monday Blues as central parts of his community work.

en.why_it_matters: For two decades, Blue Monday Blues has made live blues part of Westminster's weekly civic rhythm in Southwest DC. This night matters because the music is carrying a real transition: the 20th anniversary is also the final Blue Monday of Rev. Brian Hamilton's era, closing the chapter of a pastor whose community work helped make Westminster's jazz-and-blues nights a local institution. The lineup gives that history a live soundtrack rather than turning the evening into a ceremony about the past.
en.trip_verdict: If you are in the DMV, actively make room for this Monday at Westminster. The reason is local and cannot really be exported: the church, the Southwest community, and the end of the Hamilton chapter are part of the event itself. I would not turn it into a corridor trip from another city, because Westminster is explicitly carrying the program into a new era rather than ending Blue Monday altogether.

es.why_it_matters: Durante dos décadas, Blue Monday Blues ha convertido el blues en parte del ritmo semanal y comunitario de Westminster en Southwest DC. Esta noche importa porque la música acompaña una transición real: el 20 aniversario coincide con el último Blue Monday de la etapa del Rev. Brian Hamilton, cerrando el capítulo de un pastor cuyo trabajo comunitario ayudó a volver las noches de jazz y blues de Westminster una institución local. El cartel le pone música viva a esa historia, en vez de convertir la noche en una ceremonia sobre el pasado.
es.trip_verdict: Si estás en el DMV, sí le haría espacio activamente a ese lunes en Westminster. La razón es local y difícilmente se puede trasladar a otro lugar: la iglesia, la comunidad de Southwest y el cierre de la etapa de Hamilton forman parte del evento. No lo convertiría en un viaje por el corredor desde otra ciudad, porque Westminster habla explícitamente de pasar a una nueva era, no de terminar Blue Monday por completo.
